recipes.title: Classic Italian Tiramisu
recipes.description: A rich, creamy Italian dessert with coffee-soaked ladyfingers and mascarpone cheese. This no-bake dessert is perfect for any occasion.
instructions: Separate egg yolks and whites into two large bowls.
Beat egg yolks with sugar until pale and fluffy (about 3-4 minutes).
Add mascarpone cheese to the yolk mixture and blend until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites until stiff peaks form.
Gently fold the egg whites into the mascarpone mixture using a spatula.
Combine the espresso and Marsala wine in a shallow dish.
Quickly dip each ladyfinger into the coffee mixture (don't soak them).
Arrange a layer of soaked ladyfingers in a 9x13 inch dish.
Spread half of the mascarpone mixture over the ladyfingers.
Repeat with another layer of dipped ladyfingers and remaining mascarpone.
Dust the top generously with cocoa powder using a fine sieve.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.
Serve chilled and enjoy within 2-3 days.
recipes.author: Chef Marco Rossi

recipes.title: Molten Chocolate Lava Cake
recipes.description: Individual chocolate cakes with a gooey, molten chocolate center. The perfect romantic dessert that's surprisingly easy to make.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Butter four 6-oz ramekins generously and dust with cocoa powder.
Melt chocolate and butter together in a double boiler, stirring until smooth.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
In a separate bowl, whisk together eggs, egg yolks, and sugar until thick and pale.
Add vanilla extract and salt to the egg mixture.
Fold the melted chocolate into the egg mixture gently.
Sift in the flour and fold until just combined (don't overmix).
Divide batter evenly among the prepared ramekins.
Place ramekins on a baking sheet and bake for 12-14 minutes.
The edges should be firm but the center still soft.
Let cool for 1 minute, then carefully invert onto serving plates.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve immediately with vanilla ice cream.
recipes.author: Pastry Chef Sophie

recipes.title: Classic Crème Brûlée
recipes.description: Silky smooth French custard with a crackling caramelized sugar topping. An elegant dessert that's easier than it looks.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Split vanilla bean lengthwise and scrape out seeds.
Heat cream with vanilla bean and seeds until just simmering.
Remove from heat and let steep for 10 minutes.
Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale and thick.
Remove vanilla bean pod from cream.
Slowly pour hot cream into egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve.
Divide custard among 6 ramekins.
Place ramekins in a baking pan and fill pan with hot water halfway up sides.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until set but still slightly jiggly in center.
Remove from water bath and cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Before serving, sprinkle 1 tbsp sugar evenly over each custard.
Caramelize sugar with a kitchen torch until golden and crackling.
Let stand 2 minutes before serving.
recipes.author: Chef Pierre Dubois

recipes.title: French Macarons
recipes.description: Delicate almond meringue cookies with a smooth ganache filling. These colorful treats are the ultimate French pastry.
instructions: Sift almond flour and powdered sugar together twice.
Age egg whites at room temperature for 24 hours (or use 3-day old eggs).
Beat egg whites until foamy, then gradually add granulated sugar.
Continue beating until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Add food coloring if desired.
Fold dry ingredients into meringue in thirds using macaronage technique.
Mixture should flow like lava and form a ribbon.
Transfer to piping bag fitted with round tip.
Pipe 1.5-inch circles onto parchment-lined baking sheets.
Tap sheets firmly on counter to release air bubbles.
Let shells dry at room temperature for 30-60 minutes until skin forms.
Preheat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Bake for 13-15 minutes, rotating halfway through.
Shells should have formed feet and come off parchment easily.
Cool completely before removing from sheets.
For ganache: heat cream and pour over chopped chocolate, stir until smooth.
Cool ganache until spreadable, then pipe onto half the shells.
Sandwich with remaining shells and refrigerate for 24 hours before serving.
recipes.author: Pâtissier Laurent

recipes.title: New York Cheesecake
recipes.description: The ultimate creamy, dense cheesecake with a graham cracker crust. This iconic American dessert is rich and satisfying.
instructions: Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C).
Mix graham cracker crumbs with melted butter.
Press mixture firmly into bottom of 9-inch springform pan.
Bake crust for 10 minutes, then cool.
Beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth and fluffy (3-4 minutes).
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Mix in sour cream, vanilla, lemon juice, and flour until just combined.
Pour filling over crust.
Wrap outside of springform pan with aluminum foil.
Place in larger roasting pan and fill with hot water halfway up sides.
Bake for 55-65 minutes until edges are set but center still jiggles slightly.
Turn off oven and crack door open, let cheesecake cool in oven for 1 hour.
Remove from oven and water bath, cool to room temperature.
Refrigerate for at least 8 hours or overnight before serving.
Run a knife around edge before releasing springform.
Serve plain or with fresh berries.
recipes.author: Baker Sarah Johnson

recipes.title: Ultimate Fudgy Brownies
recipes.description: Rich, dense, and incredibly chocolatey brownies with a shiny crackly top. These are the best brownies you'll ever make.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Line a 9x13 inch pan with parchment paper.
Melt chocolate and butter together, stirring until smooth.
Remove from heat and whisk in both sugars until combined.
Let cool for 5 minutes.
Add eggs one at a time, whisking vigorously after each.
Stir in vanilla extract.
Sift together flour, cocoa powder, and salt.
Fold dry ingredients into chocolate mixture until just combined.
Pour batter into prepared pan and spread evenly.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until a toothpick comes out with moist crumbs.
Do not overbake - center should still look slightly underdone.
Cool completely in pan on wire rack.
Cut into 16 squares and serve.
Store in airtight container for up to 5 days.
recipes.author: Home Baker Emma

recipes.title: Chocolate Profiteroles
recipes.description: Light and airy choux pastry puffs filled with vanilla cream and topped with rich chocolate sauce. A show-stopping French dessert.
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a saucepan, bring water, butter, and salt to a rolling boil.
Remove from heat and add flour all at once, stirring vigorously.
Return to medium heat and stir constantly for 1-2 minutes until mixture forms a ball.
Transfer to a bowl and let cool for 5 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time until mixture is smooth and glossy.
Transfer dough to piping bag with large round tip.
Pipe 1.5-inch mounds onto baking sheets, spacing 2 inches apart.
Bake for 15 minutes at 425°F, then reduce to 375°F and bake 15 more minutes.
Do not open oven during baking!
Pierce each puff with a knife tip to release steam and cool completely.
Whip cream with powdered sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form.
Cut puffs in half and pipe cream into bottoms.
For ganache: heat cream and pour over chopped chocolate, stir until smooth.
Replace puff tops and drizzle with chocolate ganache.
Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve.
recipes.author: Chef Antoine

recipes.title: Vanilla Panna Cotta
recipes.description: Silky Italian cream dessert with a delicate wobble. This elegant no-bake dessert is easier than you think.
instructions: Sprinkle gelatin over cold water in a small bowl and let bloom for 5 minutes.
Split vanilla bean and scrape out seeds.
In a saucepan, combine cream, milk, sugar, vanilla bean and seeds.
Heat over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves and mixture is hot but not boiling.
Remove from heat and remove vanilla bean pod.
Add bloomed gelatin and stir until completely dissolved.
Strain mixture through fine-mesh sieve.
Divide among 6 ramekins or glasses.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set.
To unmold: dip ramekins in hot water for 5 seconds and invert onto plates.
Or serve directly in glasses.
Top with fresh berries, berry compote, or caramel sauce.
Serve chilled.
recipes.author: Chef Isabella Romano

recipes.title: Classic Apple Pie
recipes.description: Traditional American apple pie with flaky buttery crust and cinnamon-spiced apple filling. The ultimate comfort dessert.
instructions: For crust: combine flour and salt in a bowl.
Cut cold butter into small cubes and add to flour.
Use pastry cutter to work butter into flour until pea-sized pieces form.
Add ice water gradually, mixing until dough just comes together.
Divide dough in half, form into discs, wrap and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Peel, core, and slice apples into 1/4-inch slices.
Toss apples with both sugars, cinnamon, flour, and lemon juice.
Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C).
Roll out one dough disc and fit into 9-inch pie pan.
Fill with apple mixture, mounding slightly in center.
Roll out second dough disc for top crust.
Place over filling, trim and crimp edges.
Cut several slits in top for steam vents.
Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes, then reduce heat to 375°F and bake 35-40 minutes more.
Crust should be golden and filling bubbling.
Cool for at least 2 hours before slicing.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.
recipes.author: Baker Mary Williams

recipes.title: Authentic Italian Gelato
recipes.description: Smooth, dense Italian ice cream with intense flavor. This stracciatella version includes chocolate shavings throughout.
instructions: Split vanilla bean and scrape out seeds.
Heat milk, cream, vanilla bean and seeds in a saucepan until steaming.
Whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale and thick.
Slowly pour hot milk into egg mixture while whisking constantly.
Return mixture to saucepan and cook over medium-low heat.
Stir constantly until mixture reaches 170°F and coats back of spoon.
Do not let it boil or eggs will curdle.
Strain through fine-mesh sieve into a bowl.
Remove vanilla bean pod.
Cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Churn in ice cream maker according to manufacturer's instructions.
In last 2 minutes of churning, drizzle in melted chocolate in a thin stream.
It will harden and create chocolate chips throughout.
Transfer to container and freeze for 2-3 hours until firm.
Let stand at room temperature for 5 minutes before scooping.
Serve in chilled bowls or cones.
recipes.author: Gelatiere Giuseppe
